title: We found what looked like AI slop on Teachers Pay Teachers. Here’s what the platform did next.
key_facts: Teachers Pay Teachers (TPT), a marketplace for classroom resources, plans to ban AI-generated resources, announced at a town hall last week.
The move follows Chalkbeat reporting that found apparent AI slop for sale, such as an alphabet worksheet missing the letter F.
TPT spokeswoman Sarah Lehman said it is building tools to identify and remove AI-generated resources.
The ban drew protests, including an online petition, from sellers.
TPT also created a new seller tier with a $60 annual fee that requires exclusivity on TPT.
Teacher Nicholas Ferroni called the exclusivity change a slap in the face for teachers.
quote_evidence: Teachers Pay Teachers, a popular online marketplace among teachers for classroom resources that critics say are sometimes of dubious value, plans to ban AI-generated resources from its site.
TPT’s move to ban AI-generated resources has drawn protests, including an online petition.
why_it_matters_hint: Teaching materials may soon be checked for AI origin.
event_date: Town hall last week (before 15 Oct 2026); article 15 Oct 2026
notes: Status CONFIRMED because a TPT spokeswoman states the plan.
